threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still pronounce 'Dalston' like ‘Dahl-ston’ instead of ‘Daw-ston’. The locals can spot you a mile away.
Caught a bloke in a tattered coat singing to a plastic bag on the 36 last night. He’s got moves; I half thought he was a performance artist.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw that old man in the bakery arguing with the staff over his favorite rye bread. It's the little things, you know?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a fusion of Turkish döner and German beer at a street corner, where locals debate over the best late-night spots.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can name the taco truck that used to park by the old laundromat on 24th and don’t even flinch when BART’s down again.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today with an old-timer recounting how the routes used to go through the old Embarcadero. His stories made the 30-minute wait almost feel nostalgic.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to Park Güell, but they miss the tiny, hidden squares where locals sip vermut and chat—those moments are pure Gràcia.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still ordering a café con leche and expecting it hot, not realizing it’s served cold here after noon.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think a 'small flat white' is a standard order. Locals know to just say 'flat white' and leave the small for the tourists.
Caught a bloke singing Spice Girls loudly on the 77 last night. Whole bus joined in; even the driver was chuckling. Classic Clapham vibes.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Last week, I saw a kid selling hand-drawn flyers for a local concert in front of the bakery. That type of creativity really hit home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop that sells fresh pita bread made by an elderly Turkish lady who hums old German folk songs as she works.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they know to wear layers even in July—because the sun’s out, but that wind ain't foolin’ nobody.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Spotted a guy in a tuxedo on the 5, flipping through a stack of playbills. Only in SF do you get pre-show vibes on your evening commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think ‘Gràcia’ is just for Gaudí sights, missing the real charm in our local fiestas and tucked-away artisan shops. They skim the surface.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them at the Mercat de la Llibertat, struggling to remember the Catalan names for the fruits and vegetables while holding a smartphone.
